summary: Macro backdrop for ags: mixed (score -1 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar 0; brl 0; mxn −; risk 0; energy +; china −; breadth 0. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Coffee +13.8%; weakest: KC wheat -13.5%.

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 4.96% (+0 bp in a month), 2-year 4.65% (-6 bp); 2s10s curve +31 bp (+6 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.04% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 101.74 (+0.6% in a month, +3.5% YTD). USD/BRL 5.036 (-1.3% in a month): little changed. USD/CNY 6.660 (-0.6%); USD/MXN 18.66 (+8.0%); a sharply weaker peso cuts Mexico's buying power for US corn, pork, dairy and wheat (Mexico is the top buyer of all four).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -1.0% in a month (+11.5% YTD); VIX 20.0. Neutral risk backdrop.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 102.22 $/bbl (+14.2% in a month), Brent 111.13, ULSD 4.750 $/gal (+5.2%), natural gas 2.70 (-14.4%). Higher crude lifts biofuel margins (soybean oil, corn for ethanol) and synthetic-fibre costs (supports cotton), but raises diesel, drying and freight costs. Natural gas drives nitrogen fertilizer costs for next year's corn.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -4.0% in a month, Shanghai Composite -6.3%, Hang Seng -7.0%, yuan +0.6% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 14 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (42%); S&P GSCI +2.5% in a month; gold -6.5%.
